_readme: THE APPLY ORDER OF supabase/migrations/**. This is the single source of truth
for rebuilding the database from the repo, and it is verified on every push by
tests/schema-drift.mjs (via tests/schema-replay.mjs).
WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. Filename order does NOT replay. Measured
2026-08-14: applying supabase/schema.sql + every migration in filename order
gets 23 of 41 files in and fails the other 18. Two reasons, both structural:
1. '2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql' sorts BEFORE '2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql',
because '-' (0x2D) < '.' (0x2E). The -2 file's first act is to check that
clan_board exists and raise if it does not, so it fails first, every time.
2. Nine files are dated 2026-08-11 and alphabetical order puts 'accrual',
'accrue-gate', 'anon-execute-lockdown', 'apply-engine' and
'authenticated-surface-lockdown' all BEFORE 'player-state' — which is the
foundation every one of them depends on. There is no naming scheme that
rescues this after the fact.
Before this file, the working order existed only as a hand-maintained const
array inside tests/pglite-chain.mjs and another inside
tests/conservation-fuzz.mjs, each covering a DIFFERENT SUBSET of the
migrations, and neither one covering all of them. That means the order
required to rebuild the database was not written down anywhere.
RULES:
· Every .sql file in supabase/migrations/ must appear exactly once, across
'pre_schema', 'order' and 'excluded'. The guard FAILS on a file that is in
none of them — so a new migration cannot be silently left out of the
rebuild. The full apply sequence is: pre_schema, then supabase/schema.sql,
then order.
· A new migration goes where it actually has to run, not where its date
puts it.
· 'excluded' is a claim that a rebuilt database is CORRECT without the file.
Never add one to make the chain go green.

_why: GUCs production was actually applied with, not shortcuts.
it, and production was applied with it set on 2026-08-13 (that is what closed
A11). A rebuild that omitted it would leave beta_invites world-readable and
the file would tell you so, loudly.
market_wipe_ok: read by 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql, which is now IN 'order'.
The replay's market tables are empty, so the gate would not fire there — it
is set anyway, because the value of this map is that it records what a real
apply needs, and a real apply of that file against production DOES fire.

_pre_schema_why: supabase/schema.sql creates game_saves and game_events with `create table if
not exists` as a bootstrap fallback, and its own header says they are assumed
to already exist. Those fallback definitions do not match production: different
primary key on game_saves, different COLUMN NAMES on game_events (kind vs
event_type, created_at vs occurred_at). Running the true shapes first makes
schema.sql's fallback no-op on a rebuild exactly as it no-ops on production.
The alternative — ALTER + rename the columns afterwards — is a rename on the
table holding every player's save, which cannot be rolled forward past a
failure. Ordering is reversible; that is not.

_order_notes.2026-08-10-dr-beta-invites-base.sql: Reconstruction of a production object with no migration file. Must precede authenticated-surface-lockdown (A9's retrofit list names claim_beta_invite(text) and fails closed on it) and live-market-rls (§3 reads public.beta_invites).
_order_notes.2026-08-10-dr-bug-reports-base.sql: Reconstruction of a production object with no migration file. Must precede bug-report-relay, which ALTERs the table and creates bug_report_submit — which A9 then retrofits.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-player-state.sql: The foundation. Nine 2026-08-11 files depend on it and five of them sort before it alphabetically.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-clan-membership-authority.sql: Before clan-write-policy-pin and raid-claim-authority: all three once defined clan_members "join as self"; this file now owns the definition and the other two assert against whatever is live. Applying them the other way round silently deletes R4's timestamp pin — see HANDOFF, 'A LATENT BUG WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE THAT FOUND IT'.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdow: The A9 __ungated retrofit. Every later file that references a *__ungated name depends on it, and it in turn needs every RPC it retrofits to already exist — so it sits after the whole clan/raid/market surface and before the 08-13 files.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-daily-budget.sql: Before apply-engine: apply-engine §0 fails CLOSED without hr_day_budget_check. Applying them the other way round is a refused migration, not a slow degradation.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-grant-hygiene.sql: Last of the 08-11 block: it is the detector, so it must see the finished surface. It reports every un-retrofitted RPC, which makes it a second, independent check that A9 ran.
_order_notes.2026-08-15-auto-eat.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED to production yet — in 'order' rather than 'excluded' for the same reason 2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql is: the replay is how a staged migration gets EXECUTED before anyone applies it, and its self-verifying block is the commit gate. It REPLACES hr_state_of, so it must sit after apply-engine; it reads hr_items.auto_eatable, so the catalogue must be regenerated (it is, in this repo) and RE-APPLIED to production before this file. APPLIED to production 2026-08-15, together with the regenerated catalogue.
_order_notes.2026-08-15-activity-intent.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies), but it belongs in 'order' rather than 'excluded' because a rebuilt database SHOULD have it — same treatment as 2026-08-14-leaderboard-view-lockdown.sql. Last, and it has four real predecessors: accrue-gate (it replaces hr_rate_gate), catalogue (hr_activities), apply-engine (§0 refuses to install against an hr_apply with no intent_mismatch branch or no S5 accrued_to stamp) and character-bootstrap (§4 drives a real character).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-intent-key-hygiene.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST, and it must stay last of anything that touches hr_apply: it is a `create or replace` of the WHOLE hr_apply body, derived programmatically from 2026-08-11-apply-engine.sql (byte-identical to production, md5 917967d4bb03ca1c098b3e896a3e8317, compared 2026-08-15) and patched at four anchors. A file applied after this one that also replaces hr_apply would silently delete the C1/C3 fixes; a file applied BEFORE it that did so would be silently deleted BY it. Its §0 refuses to install against an hr_apply with no intent_mismatch branch, which is the closest a migration can get to 'do not replace a body you cannot account for'. Real predecessors: player-state (player_intents.slot), apply-engine (the body), character-bootstrap + catalogue (§4 drives two real characters).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql: APPLIED to production 2026-08-15. LAST OF THE hr_apply CHAIN, and it TAKES OVER from tool-carry as the last file that may replace hr_apply — Security's BLOCKING condition 1 on the gold-grant intent (gems had a per-call clamp and no daily ceiling; their probe minted 1.2M gems in 12 calls with zero refusals while the identical gold loop was refused at call 6). Its hr_apply body is tool-carry's, extracted programmatically and patched at four anchors, so applying tool-carry AFTER this would silently delete the gems dimension while the ledger column and hr_day_budget_check's 6-arg signature survived — the ceiling would be gone and every self-check would still pass. §0 refuses to install against an hr_apply missing any of ten named properties (b346 C1/C3, the S5 accrued_to stamp, the 12M XP clamp, b348 tool_carry), with a POSITIVE and a NEGATIVE control so a blind prosrc scan cannot report a clean bill. Real predecessors: daily-budget (it replaces all three budget functions and drops the 5-arg check), player-state (player_ledger), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene + tool-carry (the body), character-bootstrap + catalogue (§10(b) drives two real characters).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-tool-carry.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). It took over from intent-key-hygiene as the last file that may replace hr_apply, and has since been SUPERSEDED in that role by 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql — which derives its body from THIS file. Original note:
_order_notes._2026-08-15-tool-carry.sql-original: TAKES OVER from intent-key-hygiene as the last file that may replace hr_apply: its body is the b346 body, extracted programmatically and patched at four anchors, so applying intent-key-hygiene AFTER this would silently delete the tool_carry key while the Edge Function keeps proposing it — every gather accrual would then 409 with unknown_delta_key and cost a whole night. Its §0 refuses to install against an hr_apply with no `v_prev_slot` (i.e. one older than b346), which is the closest a migration can get to 'do not replace a body you cannot account for'. It also REPLACES hr_state_of, so it must follow auto-eat.sql (whose three columns its restated body reads). Real predecessors: player-state (the table), catalogue (hr_skills, which the carry validation checks against), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene (the body), auto-eat (hr_state_of), character-bootstrap (§5(b) drives a real character).
_order_notes.2026-08-16-claim-reward.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL, and it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-15-gold-intents.sql as THE LAST FILE THAT MAY `create or replace` hr_rate_gate. Its gate body is gold-intents' LANDED body — extracted programmatically from that file's create-or-replace by tools/derive-rate-gate.mjs, never retyped — patched to add ONE arm, `claim`. So the four buckets are accrue, activity, shop and claim, and its §3(C) asserts ALL FOUR BEHAVIOURALLY (gold-intents' pattern, extended) rather than asserting only the arm this file adds: a self-check that tests only its own file's terms cannot detect a later file undoing an earlier one, which is the clan_members "join as self" defect (HANDOFF, 'A LATENT BUG WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE THAT FOUND IT'). Applied BEFORE gold-intents it would silently delete the `shop` bucket and take both gold verbs offline (429, having read and written nothing), so its §0 REFUSES TO INSTALL against a live hr_rate_gate whose body lacks a `shop` arm — with a positive and a negative scan control, the gem-migration pattern, so a blind prosrc scan cannot report a clean bill. It does NOT touch hr_apply, so 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql remains the last file that may replace THAT body; its §0 instead ASSERTS the terms of intent-key-hygiene, tool-carry and gem-daily-budget against the live body (`v_prev_slot`, `tool_carry`) with a control term, and refuses to install a second client-chosen intent-id producer onto an older hr_apply. It adds exactly two objects: hr_rate_gate's `claim` arm and hr_claim_lookup. Real predecessors: accrue-gate + activity-intent + gold-intents (the gate body, in that order — the derivation chain), clan-seat (hr_utc_day_key — this file deliberately defines no second day-key function), player-state (player_progress), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene + tool-carry + gem-daily-budget (the hr_apply terms §0 asserts), progress_claim, character-bootstrap (§5 drives a real character), catalogue (hr_start_kit).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-perk-channel.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). It does NOT touch hr_apply — its only `create or replace` is on a function it introduces — so it may sit before or after tool-carry, and tool-carry remains the last file that may replace hr_apply. Placed last only because it is newest. Real predecessors: player-state (player_state + player_progress + hr_create_character, which §4(b) drives) and accrual (the hr_engine role). ⚠ IT DECLARES A SEAM, `public.hr_unlock_levels(uuid,int)`, and creates it ONLY IF ABSENT — so the unlock-storage migration may land before OR after and whichever lands first is authoritative. Do not 'tidy' that into an unconditional create-or-replace: two files defining one object in filename order is the clan_members "join as self" defect that nearly shipped.
_order_notes.2026-08-15-gold-intents.sql: APPLIED to production 2026-08-15. It is the THIRD file to `create or replace` hr_rate_gate, so it must sit after 2026-08-15-activity-intent.sql — applied the other way round it silently deletes the `activity` bucket and takes the activity intent offline, which is the clan_members "join as self" defect in miniature. Its §3(C) asserts all three buckets it knows about (accrue, activity, shop) behaviourally for exactly that reason. It is NO LONGER THE LAST such file: 2026-08-16-claim-reward.sql TAKES OVER that role, derives its gate body from THIS file's landed body, adds the `claim` arm, and asserts all FOUR buckets. Real predecessors: accrue-gate (the function), catalogue (hr_items, which §0 and §4 read), daily-budget + apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene (§0 refuses against an hr_apply with no intent_mismatch branch, no v_prev_slot slot scope, or no hr_day_budget_check call), character-bootstrap (§4 drives a real character). It does NOT touch hr_apply, so 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql (which supersedes tool-carry in that role) remains the last file that may replace it. WITHOUT IT the two gold verbs are INERT rather than broken: hr_rate_gate fails closed on an unknown bucket, so every shop_buy and vendor_sell answers 429 having read and written nothing.
_order_notes.2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). GENERATED by tools/gen-unlocks.mjs from src/data/{shops,recipes,items,perks}.js — never hand-edited; `node tools/gen-unlocks.mjs --check` is a preflight in tests/run-smoke.mjs. It creates and fills public.hr_unlocks, which is BOOKKEEPING ONLY (merge rule, storage kind, ceiling, rung ladder) and holds no game magnitude. Real predecessors: none structural — it creates its own table — but it must precede 2026-08-16-artisan-progress-model.sql, whose §0 FAILS CLOSED without it, because both hr_unlock_guard and hr_unlock_levels read the merge rule and the storage kind out of it and a guard that installs against an absent catalogue silently allows everything.
_order_notes.2026-08-16-artisan-progress-model.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL. It is THE AUTHORITATIVE DEFINITION of public.hr_unlock_levels — 2026-08-15-perk-channel.sql §1 creates that seam ONLY IF ABSENT and says whichever storage model lands first is authoritative; this is that model, and its body reads the storage KIND out of hr_unlocks rather than naming one. ⚠ Applied BEFORE perk-channel it would be the seam's author and the two would race on filename order, so its §0 REFUSES to install unless hr_perks_of already exists AND carries the b349 `sources` census. It also TAKES OVER as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_perks_of: its body is perk-channel's, extracted programmatically by tools/derive-perks-of.mjs and patched at four anchors (insertions only — PART 1f-ii grades that chain with an EMPTY declared-removals list). It does NOT touch hr_apply, so 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql remains the last file that may replace THAT body; §0 instead asserts five of its terms against the live body WITH a positive and a negative scan control, plus the BICONDITIONAL that hr_apply's progress allowlist accepts 'flag' (unlockedRecipes is unwritable without it) and refuses 'unlock' (room rungs become additively climbable with it). Real predecessors: player-state (player_progress + its kind CHECK, which §1 widens), catalogue + character-bootstrap (§8 drives a real character), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene + tool-carry + gem-daily-budget (the hr_apply terms §0 asserts and §8(c)/(l) call), perk-channel (hr_perks_of and the seam), 2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql (the catalogue). It SUPERSEDES the parked branch's 2026-08-16-unlock-grants.sql — do not merge both, or two files define hr_unlock_guard and filename order picks one, which is the clan_members "join as self" defect.
STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL, and it must stay last: it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-11-grant-hygiene.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_assert_grant_hygiene — the first file ever to take that role, since grant-hygiene had been the sole definer since 2026-08-11. It records two reviewed engine grants (hr_claim_lookup from claim-reward, hr_perks_of from perk-channel) in check (7)'s c_engine_allow, which the nightly pg_cron run currently RAISES on. Its detector body is grant-hygiene's, EXTRACTED programmatically by tools/derive-grant-hygiene.mjs and patched at ONE anchor — insertions only, so PART 1f-ii grades this chain with an EMPTY declared-removals list. Applied BEFORE claim-reward or perk-channel it would still install correctly (an allowlist is permissive) but would prove nothing, so its §4 says out loud which of the two grants the database actually has; applying grant-hygiene AFTER it would silently restore the nine-entry list and the nightly detector would start raising again on two approved grants. It must sit last for a second reason: it calls hr_assert_grant_hygiene(true), so it is the chain's end-to-end assertion that the FINISHED surface is clean — the same reason grant-hygiene sits last of the 08-11 block. Real predecessors: grant-hygiene (the body and hr_client_rpc_baseline), player-state (the hr_engine role), claim-reward + perk-channel + artisan-progress-model (the two grants its §4 clears). It adds no object, no grant and no table.
_order_notes.2026-08-16-unlock-offers.generated.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). GENERATED by tools/gen-unlock-offers.mjs from supabase/functions/hr-accrue/unlock-catalogue.js (the eligibility predicate, IMPORTED not restated), src/data/{shops,items}.js, src/legacy.js ROOMS and src/features/homestead.js TIERS; `node tools/gen-unlock-offers.mjs --check` is a preflight in tests/run-smoke.mjs. It creates and fills public.hr_unlock_offers — the PRICE and the two PREREQUISITES of every authored unlock offer, so that hr_unlock_buy can take an offer id and nothing else. It holds no game magnitude. Real predecessors: 2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql, whose merge rule and rung ladder its self-check JOINs every sellable row against (a sellable offer whose grant is not a rung the unlock catalogue knows would be sold and then refused by the storage guard — a player charged for a bad_delta), and the item catalogue, which it checks every cost line and every blueprint against. It must precede 2026-08-16-unlock-buy.sql, whose §0 FAILS CLOSED without it.
_order_notes.2026-08-16-unlock-buy.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL. It closes §9(2) of the artisan progress model: hr_unlock_buy is the ONLY writer of a kind='unlock' row, engine-only, and it takes an OFFER ID rather than a price. It does NOT touch hr_apply — 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql remains the last file that may replace that body — and §0 instead asserts four of its terms against the live body WITH a positive and a negative scan control, plus the half of the biconditional this file's existence rests on: hr_apply's progress allowlist must still REFUSE 'unlock', because a second writer added to a hole is not a fix. It TAKES OVER from 2026-08-16-engine-allowlist-claim-perks.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_assert_grant_hygiene: its detector body is THAT FILE'S, extracted by tools/derive-grant-hygiene.mjs (link 2 of the chain) and patched at the same single anchor — insertions only, so PART 1f-ii grades this link with an EMPTY declared-removals list — in order to record ONE more reviewed engine grant, the first WRITER added to that list since hr_apply. Applied BEFORE claim-perks it would silently delete the two entries that file records; §5 asserts both are still present for exactly that reason. Real predecessors: player-state (the four tables it writes), apply-engine (hr_reject/hr_record_rejection and the hr_apply terms §0 asserts), intent-key-hygiene (the slot-scoped idempotency and the version_conflict key release it copies statement for statement), clan-seat (hr_utc_day_key, for the per-day clamp — this file defines no second day-key function), unlocks.generated + artisan-progress-model (the merge rule, the storage guard trigger and hr_perks_of, which §6(b) reads the purchased rung back out of), unlock-offers.generated (price and prerequisites), character-bootstrap + catalogue (§6 drives a real character), grant-hygiene + engine-allowlist-claim-perks (the detector body and its two entries).
_order_notes.2026-08-16-client-write-grant-sweep.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL, and it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-16-unlock-buy.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_assert_grant_hygiene (Security condition C3 on b354). It does two things: it REVOKES the dead anon/authenticated write grants Security found on six content catalogues (hr_castle_*, hr_hunt_* — held back only by RLS), and it WIDENS check (4) of the detector to report any table with RLS on, NO write policy and a client write grant, minus a new public.hr_client_write_baseline recording the 21 pre-existing ones that are not swept here. Its detector body is unlock-buy's, extracted by tools/derive-grant-hygiene.mjs (LINKS[2]) and patched at ONE anchor — the FIRST link in this chain that REPLACES rather than inserts, so PART 1f-ii grades it with a four-line declared-removals list. Applied BEFORE unlock-buy it would refuse: its §0 requires all TWELVE engine-allowlist entries (nine base + claim_lookup + perks_of + hr_unlock_buy) to be live, with a positive and a negative scan control. Real predecessors: grant-hygiene (the detector and hr_client_rpc_baseline), engine-allowlist-claim-perks and unlock-buy (the body and its twelve entries), hunt + the castle tables (the six relations it revokes; absent ones are a notice, not an error).
_order_notes.2026-08-17-market-v2.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST OF ALL. It SUPERSEDES 2026-08-11-market-v2.sql, which is DELETED in the same commit — two files defining market_list/market_cancel/market_buy is the clan_members "join as self" defect, and the old one's three functions were client-callable with none of today's rules (its §11(f) asserts they are gone). It moved from 'excluded' to 'order' because the claim changed: the old file was excluded on 'a rebuild must reproduce production and production does not have it', which is the treatment for a file nobody intends to apply; this one is on the cutover path, so it gets the activity-intent/auto-eat treatment instead — in 'order', because the replay is how a staged migration gets EXECUTED before anyone applies it, and its self-verifying block is the commit gate. It TAKES OVER from 2026-08-16-client-write-grant-sweep.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_assert_grant_hygiene, recording THREE reviewed engine grants (the market verbs) via tools/derive-grant-hygiene.mjs LINKS[3] — an insertion, so PART 1f-ii grades this link with an EMPTY declared-removals list. It does NOT touch hr_apply (2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql remains the last file that may) and does NOT touch hr_rate_gate (2026-08-16-claim-reward.sql remains the last; the market verbs deliberately reuse the `apply` rate namespace rather than opening a fifth bucket — a second allowance would raise a compromised engine's total reachable write rate). §0 instead ASSERTS four hr_apply terms against the live body with a positive and a negative scan control. Real predecessors: player-state (the four tables + the rate sampler + hr_state_of), catalogue (hr_items, the tradeable allowlist), clan-seat (hr_utc_day_key, for the per-day clamps — this file defines no second day-key function), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene + tool-carry + gem-daily-budget (the hr_apply terms §0 asserts), grant-hygiene + engine-allowlist-claim-perks + unlock-buy + client-write-grant-sweep (the detector body and its twelve entries, all of which §10's derivation carries forward), character-bootstrap (tests/market-v2.mjs drives two real characters against it).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-auto-eat-baseline.sql: APPLIED to production 2026-08-15. Records hr_set_auto_eat in hr_client_rpc_baseline — the auto-eat migration granted it to authenticated without the baseline row, which is exactly what check (2) of hr_assert_grant_hygiene raises on, and that detector runs nightly on pg_cron. Must follow both auto-eat.sql (the function) and grant-hygiene.sql (the table).

excluded.2026-08-12-clan-members-rls-drop.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED, and it REFUSES to apply by design: its precondition needs a real clan_ledger row of kind='member', i.e. a player who joined through clan_join(). A fresh rebuild has no such row, so the file correctly raises. That refusal is the file working, not the chain failing.
